title: Invariant opens in a smooth presentation descend to open substacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, and $p:P\to\mathcal X$ a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Put $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with projections $s,t:R\to P$. An open substack means a strictly full substack (closed under isomorphism) whose base change by every scheme is an open subscheme; an open subspace of an algebraic space is defined by the same base-change condition. Pullback along $p$ gives an inclusion-preserving bijection between open substacks $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$ and open subschemes $V\subseteq P$ satisfying $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$ as open subspaces of $R$. The corresponding pair satisfies $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W=V$. For every morphism of algebraic stacks $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$, the map $f$ factors through $\mathcal W$ if and only if $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}P\to P$ factors through $V$. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes over $S$ with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Fibred groupoids, stacks, representability and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and surjectivity of a representable map are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary surjectivity on points. In particular, by the smooth surjective atlas condition, for each scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ the algebraic-space projection $T\times_{\mathcal X}P\to T$ is smooth and surjective.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open-substack case and factorization criterion; atlas convention of algebraic.tex, definition-algebraic-stack.

proof.text: For an open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$, its scheme test along $P\to\mathcal X$ is an open subscheme $V\subseteq P$. The two pullbacks to $R$ are the same open subspace: an $R$-object includes an isomorphism between its two images in $\mathcal X$, and membership in a strictly full substack is invariant under this isomorphism. Pulling back an inclusion of substacks gives an inclusion of these open subschemes. This proves that the proposed map is defined and preserves inclusion; it does not yet assert existence of its inverse.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), forward map; Tag 04YM (definition-substacks), strict fullness

proof.text: Fix an invariant open $V\subseteq P$. For a scheme $T$ and object $x:T\to\mathcal X$, put $Q_x=T\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with projections $q_x:Q_x\to T$ and $a_x:Q_x\to P$, and put $E_x=Q_x\times_PV$. These are algebraic spaces by representability of the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ and by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; $E_x$ is an open subspace of $Q_x$ by the scheme-test definition of an open subspace. The atlas hypothesis makes $q_x$ smooth and gives a surjective scheme chart over $T$. The current chart-test equivalence in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] therefore gives field-extension local lifting for $q_x$: each field-valued point of $T$ lifts after a field extension. Thus $|q_x|$ is surjective on point classes, in the convention of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The smooth-implies-flat-and-locally-of-finite-presentation clause of the same calculus node applies to this algebraic-space map, so [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] makes $q_x$ an open map. Consequently $U_x=|q_x|(|E_x|)$ is open in $T$. Give it its open subscheme structure, using [def-weil-open-immersion]. Open subspaces are determined by their point subsets by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]; only that node's open-subspace correspondence is used, not its etale-image theorem for the smooth map $q_x$.

source.place: Tag 042S (lemma-fppf-open); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces); chartwise smooth implies flat and locally finitely presented

proof.text: The construction satisfies $U_{x|_{T'}}=g^{-1}(U_x)$ for every scheme map $g:T'\to T$. Indeed, the tuple definition of 2-fibre product identifies $Q_{x|_{T'}}=T'\times_TQ_x$ and $E_{x|_{T'}}=T'\times_TE_x$, respecting all projections. The image of the latter in $T'$ is contained in $g^{-1}(U_x)$. Conversely, if $t'\in T'$ maps to $q_x(e)$ for $e\in|E_x|$, the field-point convention of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] says that representatives of $t'$ and $e$ have equal images in $T$ after a common field extension. They then give a point of $T'\times_TE_x$ over $t'$. Thus the two subsets are equal, hence their open subschemes are equal. An isomorphism $x\simeq y$ over $T$ similarly induces an isomorphism $Q_x\simeq Q_y$ carrying $E_x$ to $E_y$, so $U_x=U_y$.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), common-field-extension proof, written out here; algebraic.tex Tag 003R, 2-fibre-product tuples

proof.text: Invariance gives $q_x^{-1}(U_x)=E_x$ as open subspaces of $Q_x$. One inclusion follows from the definition of $U_x$. For the other, take $z\in|Q_x|$ with $q_x(z)\in U_x$ and choose $e\in|E_x|$ with $q_x(e)=q_x(z)$. After a common field extension these two representatives give a point of $Q_x\times_TQ_x$. Over that common field, write their atlas components as $p_z,p_e$ and their comparison arrows as $\alpha_z:x\xrightarrow{\sim}p(p_z)$ and $\alpha_e:x\xrightarrow{\sim}p(p_e)$. The tuple $(p_e,p_z,\alpha_z\alpha_e^{-1})$ is a point of $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$. One projection lies in $V$, so $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$ forces the other projection to lie in $V$. Thus $z\in|E_x|$. Equality of the point subsets gives equality of open subspaces by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. For $x=p$ on $T=P$, label the projections of $Q_p=R$ so that $q_p=s$ and $a_p=t$. Then $E_p=t^{-1}(V)$, so saturation gives $s^{-1}(U_p)=t^{-1}(V)=s^{-1}(V)$, where the last equality is the assumed invariance. The map $s$ is surjective by the atlas hypothesis, hence $U_p=V$.

source.place: Tag 0507, invariant-open condition; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H4 and 03BZ, explicit saturation calculation

proof.text: Define $\mathcal W(T)$ to be the full subgroupoid of $\mathcal X(T)$ on the objects $x$ for which $U_x=T$. Step 3 makes this predicate invariant under isomorphism and stable under all pullbacks. It is local for etale covers: if $\{T_i\to T\}$ is jointly surjective, then $U_x=T$ exactly when all its inverse images $U_{x|_{T_i}}$ equal $T_i$. Hence $\mathcal W$ is a strictly full substack. Explicitly, its isomorphism sheaves are those of $\mathcal X$; an etale descent datum in $\mathcal W$ descends in $\mathcal X$ to $x$, and the displayed locality puts $x$ in $\mathcal W$. For the scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$ and any $g:T'\to T$, a lift of $xg$ to $\mathcal W$ exists exactly when $g^{-1}(U_x)=T'$, equivalently when $g$ factors through the open subscheme $U_x$. A lift is a pair $(w,\alpha)$ with $w\in\mathcal W(T\prime)$ and $\alpha:w\xrightarrow{\sim}xg$. Between two such pairs $(w,\alpha)$ and $(w\prime,\alpha\prime)$, full faithfulness gives exactly one arrow, namely $(\alpha\prime)^{-1}\alpha$. Thus the lift groupoid is contractible whenever nonempty. Therefore $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$ is represented by $U_x\subseteq T$.

source.place: Tags 04YM and 0507, strictly full substack and scheme tests, expanded directly from the stack and open-immersion definitions

proof.text: The substack just constructed is algebraic. For schemes $A,B\to\mathcal W$, full faithfulness identifies $A\times_{\mathcal W}B$ with $A\times_{\mathcal X}B$, an algebraic space since the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is representable. Step 4 gives $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W=U_p=V$. For a scheme $T\to\mathcal W$ with underlying object $x$, the tuple description identifies $T\times_{\mathcal W}V$ with $E_x\subseteq Q_x$. Since $U_x=T$, step 4 says $E_x=Q_x$. Its map to $T$ is the original smooth surjective $q_x$. Thus $V\to\mathcal W$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas, and the representable diagonal and this atlas prove algebraicity according to the definition in the statement. In particular $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ is an open substack in precisely the required scheme-test sense.

source.place: Tag 0507, algebraicity of the descended open, checked directly by diagonal and atlas instead of invoking the quotient presentation

proof.text: Let $\mathcal W'$ be any open substack with pullback $V$. For a scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$ write $T'=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W'$, viewed as an open subscheme of $T$. Associating the 2-fibre-product tuples gives $Q_x\times_TT'\simeq T\times_{\mathcal X}(P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W')\simeq T\times_{\mathcal X}V=E_x$, compatibly with the inclusions into $Q_x$. The second identification uses the given atlas pullback of $\mathcal W'$, not an assumption that its scheme test is already $U_x$. Since $q_x$ is surjective, the image of this inverse-image open in $T$ is exactly $T'$, whereas the image of $E_x$ is $U_x$. Hence $T'=U_x$. Strict fullness now gives $x\in\mathcal W'(T)$ if and only if $T'=T$, equivalently $U_x=T$, so $\mathcal W'=\mathcal W$. This proves uniqueness and the bijection. If $V_1\subseteq V_2$, then $E_{1,x}\subseteq E_{2,x}$ and $U_{1,x}\subseteq U_{2,x}$ for every $x$. Therefore $U_{1,x}=T$ implies $U_{2,x}=T$, proving inclusion preservation for the inverse as well.

source.place: Tag 0507, uniqueness; scheme-test expansion of pullback and saturation; inclusion preservation

proof.text: If $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ factors through $\mathcal W$, pulling back gives a factorization of $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}P\to P$ through $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W=V$. Conversely, suppose this atlas pullback map factors through $V$. For any scheme $T$ and object $y:T\to\mathcal Y$, put $x=fy$. Base change of the assumed factorization says that $a_x:Q_x\to P$ factors through $V$, hence $E_x=Q_x$. As $q_x$ is surjective, $U_x=|q_x|(|Q_x|)=T$. Thus every object $f(y)$ belongs to $\mathcal W(T)$. Every arrow of $\mathcal Y$ is carried to an arrow of $\mathcal W$ since it is full, and cartesian pullbacks agree since it is a full fibred subcategory. The same object and arrow assignments as $f$ therefore define a morphism $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal W$ whose composite with the inclusion is $f$. This proves the criterion for arbitrary algebraic stacks $\mathcal Y$, without imposing representability on $f$.
